output.impression: Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline. Episodic memory is severely impaired (RAVLT immediate recall 3rd percentile, delayed recall 1st percentile) and recognition does not compensate (2nd percentile), consistent with a storage-type deficit. Semantic fluency (Animals, 8th percentile) and confrontation naming (Boston Naming Test, 15th percentile) are below expected norms; letter fluency (FAS, 22nd percentile), set-shifting (Trail Making B, 15th percentile) and figure copy (20th percentile) are mildly reduced. Processing speed (Trail Making A, 25th percentile) is at the lower limit of normal. Mood screen borderline (GDS 5/15); the cognitive deficits are disproportionate to it. Screening scores: MMSE 21/30, MoCA 17/30. Tested with hearing aids in place.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MMSE 21/30 with delayed recall 0/3 not improved by cues, informant-confirmed decline over two years, and loss of instrumental independence (finances taken over, driving supervised), placing the syndrome at the dementia stage
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive assessment with informant history and functional staging
action_criteria.rationale: Two years of decline reported by his wife and daughter must be measured on a validated instrument and staged by whether instrumental independence is lost before it can be attributed [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic profile with severely impaired delayed recall and recognition, plus impaired semantic fluency and naming, with a borderline mood screen that does not account for the deficits
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the cognitive profile and establish a baseline for tracking
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing, with his hearing aids in place, defines the amnestic multi-domain profile beyond the bedside screen and sets a baseline for tracking [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, electrolytes, hepatic function and inflammatory markers; HbA1c 6.9% and fasting glucose 107 mg/dL show diabetes as a vascular risk factor to manage
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid disease, B12 deficiency, syphilis, HIV and metabolic derangement are treatable contributors and must be screened before the decline is attributed to a neurodegenerative cause [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral medial temporal atrophy (MTA 3 right, 2-3 left) with temporoparietal volume loss, plus moderate small vessel disease (Fazekas 2, basal ganglia lacunes) as a vascular contribution
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with the dementia (volumetric) protocol
action_criteria.rationale: MRI shows the pattern of atrophy and the extent of cerebrovascular disease in a man with diabetes and hypertension, and excludes hydrocephalus and mass lesions [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and it is needed when the diagnosis remains uncertain after the clinical, neuropsychological and MRI assessment or when disease-modifying treatment is being considered [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No contraindicating interaction; tamsulosin adds orthostatic and syncope risk and aspirin adds gastrointestinal risk to counsel on
action_criteria.label: Check donepezil against the current medicines before starting a cholinesterase inhibitor
action_criteria.rationale: Before a cholinesterase inhibitor is started, his tamsulosin and aspirin should be reviewed for additive syncope and gastrointestinal risk; neither changes the choice, so the check is optional [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the decline to depression or to his hearing loss: the deficits are disproportionate to a GDS of 5/15 and were measured with hearing aids in place
Do not start memantine monotherapy at the mild stage (memantine is approved for moderate-to-severe AD)
required_recommendations: Obtain collateral history from an informant who knows the patient well

Address safety: the wrong turn on a familiar route calls for a formal driving evaluation (his wife already accompanies him); the car left running and doors left unlocked call for home safety measures; keep finances with his wife and arrange supervision of medicines
Disclose the diagnosis and discuss prognosis, advance directives, and treatment options with the patient and family

Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines, counseling on dizziness with tamsulosin and gastrointestinal symptoms with aspirin [NICE_NG97]

Treat the vascular contribution: blood pressure 149/84 is above target, so confirm with home readings and intensify antihypertensive treatment if sustained; check a lipid profile and start a statin (type 2 diabetes at 74 with lacunes and moderate white matter disease); keep HbA1c individualized without hypoglycemia
Reassess mood (GDS 5/15, social withdrawal) and treat depression if confirmed

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET]

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG does not contribute to the dementia work-up; his pulse is regular at 72 and he has no syncope, palpitations or conduction history
Echocardiography does not contribute; the lacunes are small-vessel lesions, not embolic infarcts, and there is no murmur or heart failure
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; there is no syncope, palpitations or embolic-pattern infarct
Head CT adds nothing when MRI is available and tolerated; MRI is the structural study for the dementia work-up

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment (as a contributor, mixed dementia)
differential.key_features: Diabetes, hypertension, former smoking, Fazekas grade 2 white matter disease and basal ganglia lacunes contribute; but the course is gradual rather than stepwise, there is no stroke history, and memory-led decline with medial temporal atrophy points to Alzheimer disease as the primary cause
No fluctuations, visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder or parkinsonism (normal tone, no cogwheeling, normal gait)
No personality change or disinhibition apart from mild irritability at his own errors; word-finding pauses without aphasia; temporoparietal and medial temporal rather than frontal atrophy
Social withdrawal and borderline GDS 5/15, but the recall deficit is not rescued by cues or recognition and the deficits are disproportionate to mood; depression may coexist

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or infectious cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: Normal TSH, B12 (310 pg/mL with normal homocysteine), folate, RPR, HIV, electrolytes and hepatic function; diabetes is controlled (HbA1c 6.9%)

key_clinical_evidence: Insidious, progressive amnestic decline with impairment in additional domains and loss of instrumental independence meets the NIA-AA 2011 clinical criteria for probable Alzheimer disease dementia; medial temporal atrophy on MRI supports the diagnosis [NIA_AA_2011]
Delayed recall that neither cueing nor recognition rescues indicates a storage-type (hippocampal) memory deficit, the typical cognitive signature of Alzheimer disease

Moderate small vessel disease without a stroke history is a common co-pathology in older adults with diabetes and hypertension; it contributes and must be treated but does not displace Alzheimer disease as the primary cause of a memory-led decline
Cholinesterase inhibitors are the first-line symptomatic treatment for mild to moderate Alzheimer dementia; memantine is for moderate or severe disease [NICE_NG97]

sequence_constraints.reason: Obtain structural imaging before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect / herniation risk, particularly in older patients
Amyloid biomarkers are interpreted against an established clinical syndrome; they are not a screening test.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Required core: structured assessment with informant and functional staging, validated neuropsychological testing, the cognitive laboratory panel, and brain MRI showing medial temporal atrophy with moderate small vessel disease. Optional: amyloid status by CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET (one conclusive test), and a donepezil interaction check.
key_educational_points: Early Alzheimer disease classically presents with progressive episodic memory loss as the predominant symptom
Concurrent cerebrovascular disease is common in elderly patients and does not exclude AD as the primary diagnosis
APOE genotype is a risk modifier and is not a diagnostic test for Alzheimer disease

CSF biomarkers (decreased Abeta42/40 with raised p-tau) or amyloid PET establish Alzheimer pathology in vivo, useful when concurrent vascular disease complicates the picture; one conclusive test is enough
Cholinesterase inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy; vascular risk factor optimization is also important in mixed presentations
Functional assessment (finances, driving, cooking) is essential for staging and safety planning

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Harold Jenkins is a 74-year-old right-handed retired postal service supervisor who presents to the neurology memory clinic accompanied by his wife, Gloria, and adult daughter, Denise, for evaluation of progressive memory difficulties that have worsened steadily over the past two years. His wife first noticed problems approximately two years ago when Mr. Jenkins began forgetting to pay several household bills, something he had managed independently and reliably for decades. Over the subsequent months, his daughter discovered multiple unopened bills in a drawer and noticed late payment notices accumulating. His wife gradually took over the finances approximately one year ago. He frequently repeats stories and questions within the same conversation, often unaware that he has already told them. His wife reports that he left the back door unlocked several times overnight, which is very uncharacteristic, and on one occasion left the car running in the driveway for over an hour after returning from the barbershop. He has become less engaged in his weekly card game with friends from the postal service, stating that he cannot keep track of the cards as well as he used to. His golf partners have mentioned that he occasionally forgets whose turn it is and has difficulty keeping score accurately. He struggled to program the new television remote control after they recently upgraded their cable service, whereas previously he was comfortable with technology. His wife notes that he occasionally puts items in unusual places, such as placing his wallet in the refrigerator and his reading glasses in the pantry. He continues to dress himself appropriately, manages his own grooming, and recognizes all family members without difficulty. He still drives for short familiar errands but his wife has started accompanying him due to one incident where he took a wrong turn coming home from church, a route he has driven for over thirty years. He has become somewhat more withdrawn socially and occasionally appears frustrated when he cannot find the right word during conversation. He denies any hallucinations, and his family has not observed any personality or behavioral changes apart from mild irritability when he is aware of his mistakes. There have been no episodes of confusion with fluctuating alertness, no tremor, no falls, and no changes in his walking. Sleep is reportedly normal, and his wife has not observed any acting out of dreams or unusual nocturnal behaviors.

neurological_exam.additional: No paratonic rigidity. No grasp reflexes. No snout or palmomental reflexes. No myoclonus. Frontal release signs absent.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin normal bilaterally. No dysmetria or intention tremor. Rapid alternating movements intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Visual fields full to confrontation. Face symmetric at rest and with activation. Hearing reduced bilaterally (known hearing loss, wearing aids). Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline, no fasciculations or atrophy.
neurological_exam.gait: Steady gait with normal base and stride. Mild hesitation on tandem gait but completes without falling. Romberg negative. No festination, no retropulsion.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place; knows month and year but states the date is three days off and gives the wrong day of the week. MMSE 21/30, losing points on recall (0/3 at 5 minutes, no improvement with cues), orientation (2 points lost), serial sevens (2 errors), pentagons (unable to draw intersecting pentagons accurately), and the three-stage command (1 point). Clock drawing shows numbers clustered on the right side with hour hand placed at the correct number but minute hand pointing to the number 10 rather than the 2 o'clock position. Naming intact for common objects, difficulty naming the band on a watch ('that thing that holds it on'). Repetition intact. Follows two-step commands but fails three-step commands. Spelling WORLD backward: 'DLROW' with self-correction to 'DLRW' (still incorrect).
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk and tone normal throughout. No cogwheel rigidity. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. No pronator drift. No tremor, asterixis, or involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis bilaterally. Patellar reflexes 2+ bilaterally. Achilles reflexes 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffman sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception in upper extremities. Mildly reduced vibration sense at bilateral great toes (consistent with age and diabetes). Proprioception intact distally.
